dedupe_keys.name: region zealand denmark trends in emergency ambulance dispatches and response times 2013 to 2022

description: This case study analyses ten years of emergency ambulance dispatches in Region Zealand, Denmark, to see whether rising demand has lengthened response times. The authors used administrative data from the regional emergency medical dispatch centre, linked with national registries, in an open-access register-based study. It covers 678,789 priority A (emergency) and B (urgent) dispatches from 1 January 2013 to 31 December 2022, stratified by the catchment areas of the region's hospitals with emergency departments, and describes patients' age and comorbidities. The article is freely available under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the underlying registry data are not public. Caveats: it describes trends, not causes, and linkage was possible only for records with a valid personal identification number. The study found that dispatches rose in absolute numbers and per 1,000 residents for both priorities and that response times increased over the period, for example priority B response times from 12 minutes 23 seconds to 15 minutes 6 seconds, with marked differences between catchment areas. Simulation uses: a validation and calibration reference for ambulance demand and capacity planning models and for emergency response scenarios with ageing populations. Related records: the Dublin Fire Brigade incident logs (data-dublin-fire-brigade-ambulance-incident-data) and the FDNY EMS dispatch data (data-nyc-fdny-ems-incident-dispatch) are public incident datasets for similar analyses.
